news.headline: Cerebras Systems (CBRS) Surges 68% in Nasdaq Debut After $5.55B IPO
news.body: AI chipmaker Cerebras priced its IPO at $185/share — well above the $150–$160 range — raising $5.55B in the largest U.S. tech IPO since Uber in 2019, then opened at $350 and closed up 68% at $311.07, pushing its market cap to ~$95B fully diluted. Demand exceeded available shares by more than 20x, reflecting intense institutional appetite for pure-play AI semiconductor exposure. The debut is seen as a bellwether ahead of expected blockbuster listings from SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic later in 2026. After-hours action saw the stock extend gains, sustaining momentum into Friday.

news.headline: Applied Materials (AMAT) Posts Record Q2 EPS of $3.51, Guides Chip Equip. +30% in 2026
news.body: Applied Materials reported record Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue of $7.91B (+11% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $3.51, crushing consensus estimates of $2.66–$2.68 EPS and $7.65–7.82B revenue. CEO Gary Dickerson said semiconductor equipment revenue is now expected to grow more than 30% in calendar 2026, citing the rapid AI data center build-out. The company also raised its quarterly dividend 15% to $0.53/share and guided Q3 revenue to $8.95B, well above prior Street expectations. Shares climbed ~2% in after-hours trading, adding to the broader semiconductor rally.

news.headline: Cisco (CSCO) Jumps 13%+ on AI 'Networking Supercycle,' Raises FY Guidance to $9B
news.body: Cisco surged more than 13% on May 14 — its best single-day gain in over two decades — after reporting Q3 results that blew past Wall Street estimates and raising its AI infrastructure and hyperscaler order guidance from $5B to $9B for the fiscal year. CEO Chuck Robbins told CNBC that surging AI demand is driving a "networking supercycle," with orders from hyperscalers accelerating sharply. The company also announced a ~5% workforce reduction (~4,000 jobs) as it pivots resources toward AI-focused silicon and optics. The move helped push the S&P 500 above 7,500 and the Dow back above 50,000 for the first time since February.

news.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) +4.4% as U.S. Clears H200 Chip Sales to 10 Chinese Firms
news.body: Reuters exclusively reported that the U.S. Commerce Department approved ~10 Chinese companies — including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, JD.com, Lenovo, and Foxconn — to purchase Nvidia's H200 AI chips, each permitted to buy up to 75,000 units. No deliveries have been made yet, as Chinese firms pulled back after guidance from Beijing, leaving the deal in limbo even as CEO Jensen Huang accompanied President Trump to the U.S.-China summit in Beijing. Nvidia closed up 4.4% on May 14, extending its monthly gain to ~15%, as markets priced in potential re-entry to China's $50B AI chip market. The approval framework also covers AMD MI-series accelerators.

news.headline: Boeing (BA) Falls ~5% as LOT Polish Airlines Sues Over 737 MAX Safety Concealment
news.body: Boeing shares dropped roughly 4.7–5% on May 14 after LOT Polish Airlines filed a lawsuit alleging the company concealed safety defects and misrepresented pilot training requirements for the 737 MAX MCAS system — described as the first direct carrier suit tied to the prior crashes. The decline came despite positive newsflow: President Trump announced China would order 200 Boeing jets during the Beijing summit, and April net orders hit 135 planes. Investors focused instead on the legal overhang, delivery shortfalls (47 jets in April vs. 50+ expected), and persistent profitability concerns, underscoring how execution risks continue to overshadow demand tailwinds.

news.headline: Trump-Xi Beijing Summit Produces 'Strategic Stability' Framework, Tariff Truce Expected
news.body: U.S. President Trump and China's Xi Jinping opened a two-day summit in Beijing on May 14, with both sides agreeing to develop a 'constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability' as the guiding framework for the next three years. Agenda items include tariffs, rare earths, Taiwan, AI, and Iran; analysts at Goldman Sachs expect China to step up purchases of U.S. farm goods, energy, and aircraft in exchange for avoiding further tariff hikes. Asia-Pacific markets traded mixed on summit day — Nikkei fell ~1%, KOSPI gained 1.75%, and the CSI 300 declined 1.68% — as investors weighed a possible formal extension of the trade truce. The summit is the first U.S. presidential visit to Beijing in nearly a decade and is closely watched by Southeast Asian exporters whose supply chains hinge on U.S.-China trade stability.

news.headline: ENEOS Acquires Chevron's $2.2bn Singapore Refinery Stake and SE Asia Downstream Assets
news.body: Japan's largest refiner, ENEOS Holdings (TSE:5020), signed share purchase agreements on May 14 to buy Chevron's 50% stake in Singapore Refining Company (290,000 bpd capacity) plus downstream fuels and lubricants businesses in Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, and Australia for $2.17 billion cash — its first refinery ownership outside Japan. The deal, financed from existing reserves and expected to close in 2027, marks a significant expansion into Southeast Asia where petroleum demand is projected to grow, offsetting Japan's structurally declining domestic market. It also directly impacts SGX-linked Singapore Refining Company and downstream equities across the region as Western oil majors continue to divest Asian downstream assets to regional players. ENEOS posted FY2025 operating profit of JPY 466.6 billion, exceeding forecasts partly due to elevated Middle East-driven crude prices.

news.headline: Samsung Hits Record High Near ₩300,000 as KOSPI Scales All-Time Peak of 7,844
news.body: Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) surged as much as 5% on May 14 to notch a fresh record high closing in on the ₩300,000 level, helping push the KOSPI to a new all-time intraday high of 7,844.01, up 2.63%. The rotation into Samsung came as SK hynix's forward PER flipped above Samsung's for the first time ever — 6.79x vs. 6.77x — signalling a valuation reset driven by SK hynix's dominant HBM market position versus Samsung's recovery narrative. South Korea's finance minister warned that a potential Samsung worker strike could cost ~₩1 trillion per day and pose a major threat to exports and financial markets. Morgan Stanley set a year-end KOSPI ceiling at 9,500, with a bullish scenario of 10,000, though overheating signals emerged as investor credit balances surpassed ₩36 trillion.

news.headline: TSMC Lifts Global Chip Market Forecast 50% to $1.5 Trillion by 2030 on AI Surge
news.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. raised its global semiconductor market forecast to exceed $1.5 trillion by 2030, up 50% from its prior $1 trillion projection, citing explosive AI and high-performance computing demand that it expects will account for 55% of the total market. At its annual technology symposium in Hsinchu on May 14, TSMC unveiled plans to build nine phases of wafer fabs and advanced packaging facilities in 2026 alone, with 2-nm and A16 chip capacity targeted at a 70% CAGR through 2028. The update sent TSMC's U.S.-listed ADR (TSM) to an all-time high near $422, lifting the Taiwan Taiex and broader Asian semiconductor equities. Markets seized on the guidance as confirmation that the AI capex supercycle remains intact, reinforcing bullish sentiment across the chip supply chain from Seoul to Taipei.

news.headline: Japan 10-Year JGB Yield Surges to 2.605%, Highest Since 1997, on BOJ Hike Bets
news.body: Japan's 10-year government bond yield touched 2.605% on May 14, its highest level since May 1997, as BOJ April meeting minutes showed several policymakers signalling a rate hike could come as early as the next meeting, with elevated oil prices from the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict intensifying inflation risks. Three of nine BOJ board members had already voted for a hike to 1% at the April meeting, and the OECD projects the policy rate could reach 2% by end-2027. The Nikkei 225 fell roughly 1% on May 14 as rising yields pressured equities, with rate-sensitive financials diverging from broader weakness. Ultra-long JGB yields are also at multi-decade highs — the 30-year at 3.82% — raising concerns about fiscal sustainability and carry-trade unwinds that could ripple across Asian markets.

news.headline: Gold Posts Weekly Loss as Hot US PPI, Rate-Hike Odds Squeeze Bulls
news.body: Gold fell below $4,700/oz for a second straight session on May 14, heading for a weekly decline after US producer prices in April surged at their fastest pace since early 2022, driven by energy and trade costs linked to the Iran war. Combined with the prior session's CPI print of 3.8% — a three-year high — markets fully priced out Fed rate cuts for 2026, with CME FedWatch now pricing a ~30% chance of a December hike. The opportunity cost pressure on non-yielding bullion is squeezing speculative longs, even as structural central-bank demand (244 tonnes in Q1 2026) remains firm.

news.headline: NGSA Sees Record 40.3 Bcf/d Summer Gas Power Burn on Coal Switching, Data-Center Load
news.body: The Natural Gas Supply Association's 2026 Summer Outlook, released May 14, projects U.S. natural gas power burn reaching a record 40.3 Bcf/d this summer, driven by low prices accelerating coal-to-gas switching and surging baseload demand from data centers. LNG exports are forecast to rise 4.3 Bcf/d year-on-year to 19.9 Bcf/d as new capacity from Plaquemines, Corpus Christi Stage 3, and Golden Pass Train 1 comes online. Despite robust supply of ~117 Bcf/d, total summer storage injections are forecast at only 1,772 Bcf versus 2,210 Bcf last summer, leaving end-of-season inventories ~106 Bcf below the five-year average and tightening the winter risk picture. Henry Hub futures near $2.88/MMBtu reflect a market pricing in below-average storage builds, with coal displacement adding structural demand that markets will monitor into Q3.

news.headline: India Doubles Gold & Silver Import Duty to 15%, Sparking Bullion Market Chaos
news.body: India's government raised effective import duties on gold and silver from 6% to 15% on May 13, doubling basic customs duty on gold to 10% and hiking the agriculture cess fivefold, pushing total levies to 18.45% including IGST. MCX gold futures surged 5.74% in a single session while silver briefly crossed ₹3 lakh per kg—a gain of over ₹17,000/kg overnight. The move was triggered by a ballooning precious-metals import bill of $102.5 billion in FY2025-26 and pressure on India's current account amid the West Asia crisis and a rupee that hit a record low of ₹95.75 per dollar. Global silver on COMEX rose ~2.1% in sympathy while analysts warned the duty reversal could revive smuggling and distort trade flows through the India-UAE CEPA quota route.

news.headline: IEA May OMR: Global Oil Deficit to Persist Through Q3 as Hormuz Losses Mount
news.body: The IEA's May Oil Market Report warns the global oil market will remain severely undersupplied until Q4 2026, even if the US-Iran conflict ends by early June. Global oil supply fell a further 1.8 mb/d in April to 95.1 mb/d, taking total losses since February to 12.8 mb/d, with Gulf producers running 14.4 mb/d below pre-war levels. Inventories are drawing at a record pace — an estimated 8.5 mb/d deficit in Q2 — keeping Brent around $106/bbl. The report also cut its full-year demand forecast by 1.3 mb/d versus the pre-war outlook, citing demand destruction in petrochemicals and aviation.

news.headline: EIA Weekly: US Crude Stocks Fall 4.3 mb — Nearly Double Expectations
news.body: EIA data for the week ending May 8, 2026 showed US crude inventories fell by 4.3 million barrels, nearly double market expectations, reinforcing the global supply-tightness narrative. Distillate inventories posted their first increase since March (+190,000 barrels), offering marginal relief on the product side. The draw extended a run of outsized crude stock declines attributed to surge in export demand as Atlantic Basin buyers scramble to replace disrupted Hormuz-route barrels. WTI held around $100–$102/bbl in the session following the report.
